data.body: Janitor validation redesign - correction to the intent check. The intent check must NOT veto. A prior project decision is an N of 1 and may be reversed with good cause; treating 'the record says this was deliberate' as blocking would make the janitor structurally unable to recommend undoing a decision that aged badly, which is most of its purpose. Revised: the check produces a prior_decision record the proposal must ENGAGE, not obey. A reversal is legitimate when it names (a) the decision, (b) what evidence has changed since, (c) why the original reasoning no longer holds. Missing (b) is an UNINFORMED reversal and is what gets flagged. Tested against both observed failures: item 16 (persist close reason) fails on (b) - ed13 was recent and nothing had changed, correct block. Item 19 permits the outcome actually reached - wiring SupportsIncremental for both Jira providers DID supersede ce4d's negative-fixture framing, with cause, so the same mechanism blocks the uninformed reversal and permits the informed one. Corollary for divergence: neither record is authoritative. Project record = high context-fit, low statistical weight, may be stale. Community record = high statistical weight, low context-fit, may be cargo-culted - the ARG survey's dominant 'excluded at adoption' bucket is precisely a population that never tested its own prediction.
